statement: Before removing the Newtonsoft family, every parameterised serialization fixture was re-pointed at the serializers the product keeps, so a capability test could not disappear as a side effect.

fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.subject: The serializer honours the Json.NET JsonConverter attribute.
fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.reason: Both the attribute and the converter base type belong to the removed library. The subject is the removed item itself, not a ServiceBus capability.

fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.subject: The serializer honours the Json.NET JsonConverter attribute on a property.
fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.reason: Same subject as above, on a property instead of a class.

fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.subject: A protobuf generated message keeps its repeated field through serialization.
fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.reason: Re-pointing it at the kept serializer was tried and measured, not assumed. It fails: the repeated field comes back with zero entries.
fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.measurement: Serializing_a_protocol_buffer_message(SystemTextJsonMessageSerializer).Should_return_the_array_values -> Expected: property Count equal to 2, But was: 0
fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.cause: Trades is a getter only pbc::RepeatedField<T> over a readonly field (TradesBookedViciOneServiceBus.proto.cs:80-84). Json.NET populates an existing collection instance through its getter; System.Text.Json needs a setter or a constructor parameter and skips the property.
fixturesWithoutAnyKeptParameter.consequence: This is a behaviour of the removed library, not a defect of the kept serializer. It is reported as an impact of the decided removal: a consumer whose messages expose getter only collections will receive them empty once the Newtonsoft family is gone.
